name_reason: Renamed to ch27_portrait_cutscene (category ai_setup/cinematic -> portrait_cinematic). Body is two fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash calls (2nd via the wrap thunk it tail-JMPs into) at tiles (3,0x1B)/id 1 and (0xF,0x1B)/id 2 -- a portrait white-flash reveal, no dialog, no combat_aux_block AI-flag write, so the earlier '_ai_ctrl' was a false label. '_cinematic' also put it in the wrong family: the codebase reserves cinematic/cinematic_no_dialog for camera-pan establishing shots (0x36/0x39) and portrait_cutscene/portrait_cinematic for white-flash portrait reveals (structural twins 0x34/0x48, identical callee). dispatch idx 0x3F (@0x51C8D), ch27 slot 0 is turn=0xFF, dynamically armed by tile-step handler 0x3E.
purpose: Chapter 27 per-event handler (dispatch idx 0x3F), turn-event slot 0 at the turn=0xFF sentinel marker: plays a 2-portrait white-flash cinematic reveal. No AI control, no dialog.
logic_summary: Stack-frame __CHK(0x10). Calls fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash(3, 0x1B, 1) for the first portrait reveal at tile (3,0x1B) with portrait-group id 1, then issues the second reveal at tile (0xF,0x1B) with id 2 via fd2_wrap_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash(0xF, 0x1B, 2). In the binary the second reveal is reached by pushing its 3 args and tail-JMPing into the wrap thunk @ 0x35318 so the handler borrows that thunk's 0xC-byte cleanup tail; the thunk forwards straight to the cinematic helper @ 0x35822 (pan -> portrait swap -> white palette flash -> composite -> 400ms hold). The dispatch ABI passes 1 arg (event_arg) which this handler does not read; the decompiler's in_stack_00000000 / in_stack_00000008 are tail-call stack residue, not real reads.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch-table ABI argument (1-arg cdecl void fn(uint event_arg)) passed by the chapter-event dispatcher. This handler does not read it (body casts it to void).
params.reason: Name 'event_arg' accurately describes the dispatch-ABI argument and carries no address residue; unused-but-present is the standard shape for the 1-arg cdecl handler-table signature.
